alt.en: Illustrated sequence of Mune-gatame, the chest hold.

image.source: Compiled club reference document supplied by the project owner; original source not recorded

about.en: Chest on chest from the side, arms hugging around uke's trunk and far arm: the simplest-feeling of the side holds, kept by weight and hip movement rather than any particular grip.

en: Chest glued to chest, at right angles from their side
Hug around the trunk and far shoulder, elbows tight
Hips low or knees tucked; follow every bridge with your weight
Your partner lies on their back; come to their right side at right angles, chest facing down onto their chest.
Wrap your arms around their trunk and far shoulder, hugging them to you, elbows drawn in tight.
Keep your hips low to the mat, legs sprawled wide behind you, or tuck your knees against their side.
Press your chest down through theirs and keep your head low on the far side.
When they bridge, let your hips float and re-settle; when they turn, slide around them keeping chest contact unbroken.

receiving.en: A broad hugging weight lands across your chest with nothing obvious to attack: no collar grip, no head wrap, just heaviness. Bridges lift them but do not move them unless you turn as you bridge; work an elbow inside and turn towards them. Breathe steadily and tap clearly if you are held and need to stop.

viNotes.en: The simplest of the side holds to keep without sight, because there are no grips to find: your arms wrap the trunk and your chest does the work. Everything they try reads through the chest, a bridge as a lift and a turn as a roll away from you, and the answer to both is to float and settle. Slide around them with the chest contact unbroken rather than releasing and re-taking.

cue.en: Chest pressed on chest from the side, both arms hugging around the opponent's trunk and far arm.
